after: ## Six teaching phases, three reporting levels
alt: Two separate scales. Six teaching phases form a continuum that each student moves through individually and that does not match age groups or MYP years. Three reporting levels, emergent, capable and proficient, give a summative course result where a school offers eAssessment. They serve different purposes and are not the same scale.
caption: Phases track learning in class; levels report the result. Do not treat them as one scale.

after: ## The four criteria are independently weighted
alt: Each criterion, A listening, B reading, C speaking and D writing, is scored 0 to 8 for classroom assessment, giving a total of 0 to 32. Separately, the eAssessment blueprint gives each criterion 24 raw marks: A, B and D in the on-screen paper and C in a separate, internally marked, IB-moderated speaking examination.
caption: Levels 0–8 in class; 24 raw marks each in eAssessment. Do not mix the scales.

after: ## Worked example: matching preparation to level
alt: Writing expectations by level: emergent, simple sentences, basic vocabulary and formulaic expressions; capable, a range of structures, more precise vocabulary and register awareness; proficient, complex nuanced structures, idiom and sophisticated audience awareness. A capable student should target the capable column rather than under- or over-reaching.
caption: Neither under-reach nor over-reach: practise what your own level expects.

alt: Listening, reading and writing share one on-screen paper and can be revised together; speaking is a separate strand. Each is worth 24 marks. Speaking needs its own routine of spontaneous, interactive conversation under time pressure, and over-investing in writing can hide a gap in speaking.
caption: Equal weights mean no single skill should dominate revision.

alt: A decision flow: Language Acquisition is compulsory in every MYP year, except for bilingual students studying multiple languages in the Language and Literature subject group instead. Both routes lead on to DP Language Acquisition or DP Studies in Language and Literature, where audience-and-purpose writing and unscripted speaking carry over.
caption: Check your pathway first; strong criterion habits carry into either DP route.
